object: one made-up bill stepped through the three moments that decide trust in a payment: the approval, the catch before money moves, and the confirmation, each tied to the case where the same rule was used
desc: A short path through Allen Kang's work: split transactions redesigned with accountants, an A/B test that took fee opt-in from 75% to 92%, and one design system for three merged products.
lede: I’m Allen, a senior product designer in Toronto. Eight years designing, the last five on payments and finance tools: split transactions, checkout fees, and one design system for three merged products. I learn the rules from the accountants who live with them, and I build working prototypes with AI coding tools when a mock can’t settle it.
caption: One bill on its way out, sketched from the outside. Step through it.
h1: I redesigned split transactions for accountants and cut categorization tickets by 70%.
contact: If the bill above gets an approval wrong, I’d like to hear how your customers really pay.
